A0229.title: VLA Adversarial Training & Robustness
A0229.definition: Improving the robustness of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and Vision-Language Models (VLM) against adversarial inputs, backdoors, and jailbreaks via adversarial training, adversarial-example detection, cross-modal consistency constraints, and red-team assessment.
A0229.description: VLA adversarial training and robustness defend against model-level attacks such as RoboPAIR jailbreak, UPA-RFAS adversarial patches, DropVLA backdoor, and CrossInject cross-modal injection by constructing a multi-dimensional defense. First, adversarial samples (physical adversarial patches, cross-modal perturbations, jailbreak prompts) are introduced during training to perform adversarial training, improving model robustness against known attacks. Second, adversarial sample detectors are deployed to identify abnormal perturbations and injection features in inputs. Third, cross-modal consistency constraints verify the semantic consistency of outputs across visual, language, and action modalities to detect cross-modal injections. Fourth, red-team evaluation periodically conducts jailbreak and adversarial testing on deployed VLA models using methods such as RoboPAIR. This measure belongs to the same model security system as A0178 (AIoT model security protection) and A0072 (algorithm auditing mechanism), but is specifically tailored to physical-world adversarial and jailbreak scenarios for VLA/VLM, representing the core distinction of embodied intelligence defense compared to traditional AI model defense.
A0229.limitation: Adversarial training struggles to cover novel attack forms in open physical worlds, facing a 'whack-a-mole' dilemma. There is a trade-off between robustness and task performance, where excessive defense may reduce task success rates. Backdoor triggers are highly stealthy and difficult to fully detect and eliminate. Red-team evaluation is costly and cannot guarantee coverage of all attack paths.
